## Welcome

I am a PhD student in physics at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, working at the intersection of **string theory**, **condensed matter physics**, and **machine learning**. My research spans geometric engineering of supersymmetric gauge theories, Monte Carlo simulations of quantum many-body systems, and applications of modern generative models to physics problems.

I am particularly interested in how mathematical structures—from Calabi-Yau manifolds to tensor networks—illuminate the physics of strongly coupled systems. Whether through the geometry of brane tilings or the entanglement structure of critical systems, I seek unifying perspectives that connect seemingly disparate areas of physics.

---

## Research Highlights

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" icon=false}
### String Theory & Geometric Engineering
Constructing 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ SCFTs via toric Calabi-Yau orientifolds, exploring the interplay of D-branes, orientifold planes, and discrete torsion.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" icon=false}
### Condensed Matter & Many-Body Physics
Studying boundary RG flows in interacting Majorana chains using DMRG, and developing efficient Monte Carlo algorithms for long-range Coulomb interactions.
:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal" icon=false}
### Machine Learning & Generative Models
Exploring diffusion models and normalizing flows for sampling complex distributions in statistical physics and quantum field theory.
:::
